study: Humphrey et al. 2018, Good Behaviour Game (EEF efficacy trial)
eval_evidence: Report explicitly lists 'Independent evaluators: University of Manchester' (Humphrey et al.); the program was delivered by Mentor UK (delivery organisation) under licence from the American Institutes for Research, separate from the evaluation team. EEF independent-evaluator model.
developer_evidence: GBG was delivered by trained GBG coaches employed by Mentor UK (the delivery organisation), supported/licensed by AIR; teachers were trained 'by coaches ... contracted by Mentor, and trained by AIR.' Neither the evaluators nor the program licensor (AIR) delivered directly to teachers.
cascade_evidence: Transmission runs AIR (licensor, holds GBG under licence) -> trains Mentor UK coaches -> coaches train and support teachers: >=1 extra hop (train-the-trainer cascade).
counterfactual_evidence: Two-armed RCT; control schools ('usual provision' arm) continued normal practices. Business-as-usual, no active alternative behaviour program assigned.
coaching_evidence: Each school was allocated a GBG coach who 'paid approximately monthly visits to support their implementation throughout the trial', monthly coach visits 'typically involve an observation' followed by feedback — recurring in-class coaching (monthly cadence).
student_dose_evidence: GBG is a universal classroom behaviour-management game embedded in regular instruction; it changes the teacher's classroom management, with no tutoring/pull-out/extra-minutes or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Two-year intervention (Sept 2015-July 2017); the primary reading outcome (HGRT) is measured at the end of the second implementation year (T3), so by the outcome wave teachers had >=1 prior year of GBG experience. (Program designed as a fixed 2-year intervention; coded mature for the end-of-program measurement wave.)
